Python vs Java vs Go vs C: how many tokens the same code costs

The same two programs cost 809 GPT tokens in Python and 1,536 in C (+90%). Python and Ruby were the cheapest languages on every tokenizer we tested; Go and C were the most expensive. Claude 5.5 needed 43% to 59% more tokens than GPT for the same code.

Measured 2026-10-18 · 10 languages · 2 programs · 4 tokenizers · License CC BY 4.0 · Related: token cost by data format

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23446563 · Also on Hugging Face · Kaggle · GitHub

⬇ CSV ⬇ JSON (with all 20 source files) How to cite
Count the tokens in your own text → Paste your prompt and see tokens, characters and API cost on GPT, Claude and Gemini. Free and private: it runs in your browser.

Key findings

  • Python and Ruby are the cheapest. Both programs together cost 809 GPT tokens in Python and 819 in Ruby. JavaScript needs +20%, Java +50%, Go +68% and C +90%.
  • The ranking holds on every tokenizer. Python and Ruby stay at the top and Go and C at the bottom on Claude 5.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini and GPT alike.
  • Claude 5.5 costs 43% to 59% more than GPT for the same code. The gap is largest for Java (+59%). Gemini sits between them at 12% to 25% more than GPT.
  • Types add tokens. TypeScript needs 11% more GPT tokens than the same JavaScript.
  • File size is a rough guide only. Java has the most characters (5,101), but Go and C need more tokens. Characters and lines do not map neatly onto tokens.

Method

  • Two programs written in each language: an inventory class (add, restock, sell, a low-stock list, total value and a formatted report) and Dijkstra's shortest path on a 6-node graph with path reconstruction. Every version was compiled or run and printed exactly the same output as the Python version.
  • Code is idiomatic for each language with no comments: for example Java uses PriorityQueue, Go uses container/heap, and C uses a simple array scan instead of a heap. All 20 source files are in the JSON download.
  • Claude: each file sent through Claude Code (claude -p) with a fixed one-line system prompt; reported input tokens minus the same run with a one-character message. Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 gave identical counts, and a re-run gave identical counts.
  • Gemini: Google AI Studio prompt token counter on Gemini 3.8 Flash, minus its one start token. Four files were measured twice with identical results.
  • GPT: tiktoken with o200k_base.

Limitations

  • Two small programs. Real projects with comments, long names or heavy boilerplate can shift the numbers; the ranking is more stable than the exact percentages.
  • Style matters: the same language written more tersely or more verbosely will cost a different number of tokens.
  • Input tokens only; it does not measure how well each model writes or understands each language.
